note: Re-pinned at #954 stage 5 (window=0): the retirement PR deliberately reroutes the four retiring engines' cues and edits their corpus rows, so the subset digest moved once, disclosed in that PR body. Re-pinned again for the web-research split: the lookup half of the engine's triggers became its own skill, so the four pinned cases whose messages are lookups follow them. Their expected next_action and response_kind are unchanged; only the workflow name moves. Re-pinned a fourth time for the #1607 row-schema widening. This re-pin is a different kind from the three above it: no route, no expectation and no observed value changed, only the shape of the `expected` block every intervention row carries. `observed_digest` exists so the next author does not have to reconstruct that distinction. Measured: a new case-dataclass field moves `digest` alone; a pinned message reworded to the same route moves `digest` alone (the row carries `message_sha256`); a pinned message that reaches a different route moves both. A re-pin that moves `observed_digest` is a behaviour change and belongs in the PR body with the rows named. Re-pinned a fifth time at #1691: `best-practice-research` retired into `web-research`, so the pinned sibling-pointer row changes owner the same way the four lookup rows did at the split. `observed_digest` moves with it because the verdict really is different -- that is the behaviour change this PR is for, and it is exactly one row. Re-pinned a sixth time at #1839 for the wrapper card-copy voice rewrite. This one moves `observed_digest` while no verdict moves, which the measured table above did not allow for: `observed` carries `plain_headline`, and the card chooses its headline after the route rather than the router returning it. So the table gains a fourth line -- a pinned card's headline reworded to the same route moves both digests -- and the narrowness claim in `observed_serialization` is corrected to match what the projection actually carries. Narrowing the projection instead, so that claim becomes true again, would cost no coverage (`digest` hashes the whole row, headline included) and is left to this guard's owner rather than decided inside a copy PR. Re-pinned for shortlist-first routing (dispatch only on strong evidence): exactly four pinned rows move, all dispatch -> clarify, all re-pinned intervention cases (three whose intended skill leads the shortlist; greenfield-build-reaches-interview, whose does not, is recorded as a finding in its comment) -- greenfield-build-reaches-interview, jit-learn-negative-curriculum-design, jit-learn-negative-postmortem-report-rollback, jit-learn-negative-research. Fields moved: route_action, route_workflow, route_reason, plain_headline, claim_boundary, and mode/next_action/response_kind/handoff_action_count where the dispatched card had them; expected blocks move with the re-pin. No other pinned row changes, verified by per-field row diff against origin/main 4f8294f3. Re-pinned for the routing reach round: exactly one pinned row moves, korean-hermes-update-check-guide, whose cue the audit removed from parallel-tools, from dispatch to clarify. Fields moved: expected route_action, workflow, next_action and response_kind, and observed mode, route fields, claim_boundary and plain_headline. No other pinned row changes, verified by per-field row diff against origin/main f8d0ee116.
observed_serialization: sha256 over json.dumps([{'id': ..., 'observed': ...} for each pinned row sorted by id], sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode(). Narrower than `digest`: it drops the `expected` block and `message_sha256`, so it does not move when the row schema widens or when a pinned message is reworded to the same route. It is not narrower than the card, though -- `observed` carries `plain_headline` and `claim_boundary`, so a copy rewrite moves it with no route change (measured at #1839). Read a move here as "a pinned row's card output changed", and let the per-field row diff against the pre-change tree say whether the route moved or only the text did.
